$comment: Terrain pieces (spec pass S1 draft, 2026-11-02; docs/design/spec-s1-water.md section 9). DRAFT: not loaded yet; the implementer moves it to data/rules/ with a schema. Integers only, mm and L/s. Settled: the 100 m buffer from deployment zones, measured zone edge to nearest footprint edge (brief 2026-10-08; designer-placed pieces exempt, plan section 10); no full traps and the 2x route cap through the reachability check (brief 2026-10-09). All sizes and limits are proposals, hence status placeholder. Prices wait for S5. Height edits apply before tick 0 in heightEditOrder (channels and hollows by min, then ridges by max, then boulders), so plan order never changes the result.

pieces.$comment: Palette: routes a river toward or away from a ford; floods later with rain (staple 5, moat opening). Bed follows the original ground (relative depth). Side cells at half depth: a 2000 mm channel has 667 permille steps, so foot and horse cross it dry, wheeled only up to 750 mm deep (decision D8); swept soldiers can climb out at the sides (decision D10). Spoil vanishes. Allowed in water.

Palette: high ground for archers. Height stays under hazards.json lethalDropMm (4000), so a ridge is never a cliff. 400 permille sides: foot and horse climb, wheeled goes around (decision D8). Refused where any footprint cell has tick-0 water of 5 mm or more (decision D5; dams are their own piece in S3). A 3 m ridge is about 18 m wide at the base.
Optional (decision D6): the ridge's negative, applied by min. Palette: a hollow that collects floodwater. Dry ground only.

Palette: open a spring on a hillside to flood a valley floor gradually. Terrain, never timed: flows from tick 0 to the end of the battle. Its water is battle-created and skips the placement reachability check (decision D4); maxDischargeLPerS caps it (3000 L/s is 540 m3 over a 3-minute battle). Dry ground only, not on a boulder. The footprint (for the buffer) is the source block; its water may flow into the buffer as a consequence.

Palette: hard blockers that funnel the column; fire can't clear them; in a stream they dam it. One boulder per placement, 2x2 cells, grid-aligned. Closed to every class (brief 2026-10-09 lists boulders as hard blockers). Solid to water below its top; water deeper than heightMm flows over. Allowed in water (decision D5). Static in M3; rolling with a tremor arrives in M6 (brief 2026-10-11). Engineers clear small boulders (M5).
